subject: Re: Purpose-limited ML improvement clause — narrowing training rights
messages:
From: Lauren Burke <lauren.burke@medxhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: MedX Health Legal <legal@medxhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed DPA redlines re: ML training

Hi Irene,

Thanks for sending the DPA. Attached are MedX's redlines (DPA_v3_redlines.pdf). Our legal team has a couple of focused asks before we can sign:

- Narrow "Model Improvement" rights so Redwood cannot use Customer Content directly to train general-purpose models. MedX will accept aggregate, anonymized derivatives but wants an explicit prohibition on training on identifiable or customer-specific content.
- Define terms: "Customer Content", "Anonymized Aggregate Data", and "Derived Data" so there's no ambiguity.
- Subprocessor flow: we need a notification + 30-day objection period for new subprocessors that could access Customer Content.
- Cross-border transfers: any model improvement pipeline that moves data outside the US must have SCCs or equivalent and be disclosed.

We appreciate the prior conversations about opt-outs, but legal wants the above memorialized in the DPA with a clear execution path (DocuSign). We attached an SOW that describes the ML use cases — this clarifies what MedX considers "sensitive content".

Can your team propose specific language for a "Purpose-limited ML Improvement" clause that (a) allows aggregate anonymized improvements, (b) prohibits training on Customer Content, and (c) preserves the ability for MedX to opt-in for specific experiments under separate written consent?

We are trying to close this week — please let us know a time for a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Lauren Burke
Head of Legal
MedX Health

Attachments: DPA_v3_redlines.pdf (PDF, 248 KB), SOW_ML_use_case.xlsx (Excel, 62 KB)

Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines re: ML training

Hi Lauren — thanks for the redlines and the SOW, very helpful. I looped in Marissa (sales) and Karthik (privacy/compliance) so we can align on legal and commercial timelines.

High-level: Redwood's default position is to avoid training on identifiable Customer Content without explicit consent. We can propose language that narrows the "Model Improvement" right to: 1) anonymized, aggregated derivatives ("Anonymized Aggregate Data") and 2) metrics/telemetry used to improve serving quality (latency, safety heuristics) that do not retain or expose Customer Content.

Proposed next steps / specific language we can prepare for DocuSign:
- Definition block: we will add explicit definitions for "Customer Content", "Derived Data" (non-identifiable transformations), and "Anonymized Aggregate Data" (irreversibly de-identified statistical aggregates).
- Training prohibition: insert a clause along the lines of: "Provider shall not use Customer Content to train or fine-tune models intended for general public release or third-party sale, except with Customer's prior written consent."
- Opt-in experiments: a short clause to allow separate written consent for experiments scoped in a signed addendum (eg. narrow experiment, timebox, dataset retention).
- Subprocessors: we can accept a notification + 30-day objection period model for subprocessors that have access to raw Customer Content; for infra-only subprocessors with no access, we can document names and change process.
- Transfers: we will ensure SCCs or equivalent where data flows cross borders and disclose any model-training pipelines used for aggregate improvements.

I will draft proposed redline language and attach it here; if that looks good to you, we can route to DocuSign. If you prefer, we can hop on a 20-minute call today to finalize.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Irene/Team,

Thanks for the quick reply and the constructive approach. A few clarifications from MedX legal after reviewing your summary:

1) The explicit prohibition needs the phrase "no training on Customer Content" (we are trying to avoid language that could be read as allowing derivative uses that effectively reproduce customer data).
2) For transparency, MedX asks for a short quarterly notice of any model improvement programs that used Anonymized Aggregate Data derived from MedX (high level: program name, start/end dates, and whether any new subprocessors were engaged).
3) Data residency: any Customer Content used as part of an experiment must remain within US-hosted infrastructure unless MedX provides written consent.

If Redwood can accept the above edits, MedX is ready to sign on DocuSign. Our legal can turn around the final review within 48 hours. Please send your redlined DPA with the proposed definitions and the DocuSign link and I'll confirm execution.

Best,
Lauren Burke
